newsitem.title: USA: U.S. considering lifting Lebanon travel ban.
newsitem.headline: U.S. considering lifting Lebanon travel ban.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright is considering lifting a ban on U.S. citizens visiting Lebanon, provided Beirut pledges to do more to fight terrorism, a senior U.S. official said on Tuesday.

The official said Albright had not made a final decision but was "inclined to lift the restriction providing there are positive steps by the Lebanese". She was expected to take action in the next 24 hours, he added.

The ban, in force since the mid-1980s, is not total, barring American citizens only from using their U.S. passports to visit Lebanon. It is based on a judgment that Americans face a serious security threat in Lebanon -- a claim disputed by the Lebanese government.

The U.S. official said steps Lebanon could take to fight terrorism included having its parliament approve the last of 10 covenants on terrorism and hostage-taking, and designating an envoy to discuss anti-terrorism moves with a U.S. team.

The official, speaking on condition he was not identified, said that Albright, who is travelling in Asia, had telephoned Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri earlier on Tuesday and was expected to make further contacts before announcing a decision.

He said that if the ban was lifted, it was expected to be replaced by a strong travel warning telling Americans that Lebanon was still a dangerous place in which the U.S. embassy had only limited scope for helping them.
